title: Fire on Carmel (1 Kings 18)
hookLine: Elijah on Mount Carmel, where Carmelites later trace their roots

lines: THE GOD WHO ANSWERS BY FIRE.
cards: The third year of the drought. King Ahab calls Elijah the troubler of Israel, and Elijah answers: it's you who troubled Israel, by following Baal. Then he makes a proposal.
Gather everyone on Mount Carmel, the ridge above the sea. Bring the prophets of Baal, four hundred and fifty of them. And there, in front of the whole nation, we'll settle it.
Two altars, two bulls, no fire. Each side calls on its God. The God who answers by fire, he is God.
And the people, the Douay-Rheims says, answered: "A very good proposal."

teach.b: Before any fire, Elijah turns to the crowd. In the Douay: "How long do you halt between two sides? if the Lord be God, follow him." To halt is to limp.

Some readers hear in the Hebrew someone hobbling back and forth between two paths, never putting full weight on either. The people had not quite rejected the God of Israel. They just kept Baal on the side, in case.
And they answered him not a word. Then the contest.

teach.h: NO VOICE FROM MORNING TILL NOON.
teach.b: The prophets of Baal call from morning till noon, and there is no voice, no answer.
Elijah rebuilds the Lord's broken-down altar with twelve stones, one for each tribe, and has it soaked with water three times, until the trench overflows.

He prays simply: let this people know that thou art the Lord God, and that thou hast turned their heart again. The fire of the Lord falls and burns up the offering, the wood, the stones, even the water in the trench.
The people fall on their faces: the Lord he is God. Then Elijah climbs to the top of Carmel, puts his face between his knees, and sends his servant to look at the sea seven times.
On the seventh: a little cloud, like a man's foot. Then the rain.
Centuries later, hermits settled on Mount Carmel, tradition says near a spring named for Elijah.
They became the Carmelites, the order of Saint Teresa of Avila, Saint John of the Cross and Saint Thérèse of Lisieux, and they honor Elijah as their spiritual father.
Carmelite tradition even saw in that little rising cloud a figure of Mary.

how: Carmelite friars, nuns and lay Carmelites honor Elijah as their spiritual father and keep his feast, and Catholics who wear the brown scapular do so in honor of Our Lady of Mount Carmel.

the hill where Solomon built the Temple
the mountain where fire fell on Elijah's altar

he had it soaked three times until the trench was full.
the Carmelite order traces its roots to hermits on Mount Carmel
tradition places them near a spring named for Elijah, and they honor him as their father.
the people answered Elijah's challenge right away
when he asked how long they would halt, they answered him not a word.

games.q: you're Elijah. the prophets of Baal have called all morning and nothing has happened. it's your turn. what do you do with the altar?
o: light a small fire to help it along.
soak it with water three times.
pray at length before you touch it.
games.why: he drenches it until the trench overflows, then prays a short prayer. the fire of the Lord falls and licks up even the water.

practice: Go somewhere a little higher, a hill, a top-floor window, even a step, or just picture Carmel, the ridge above the sea.
Ask yourself Elijah's question, where am I limping between two sides, and don't answer it out loud yet; just notice where your weight is. If you pray, do as Elijah did, head bowed, and wait.

wordCard.voice: Carmel. The mountain where Elijah's contest proved the Lord answers by fire, and where the Carmelites later found their roots. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: Carmel, garden land or orchard. The ridge gave its name to the Carmelite order.

carryVoice: Your line: how long will you halt. One side, with your full weight. Until tomorrow.
